# ScopeView

> Small Canvas charts with exact source readings and zero runtime dependencies (`@scopedb/scopeview`).

ScopeView turns structured telemetry documents (`line`, `bar`, `area`, `scatter`, `donut`, `top-list`, `treemap`, `trace`, `profile`, `scalar`) into standalone self-contained HTML reports or lightweight browser Canvas charts without rounding away 64-bit integers, sub-millisecond nanoseconds, or distinguishing `null` from `0`.

## Agent & CLI Workflow

Install once (`npm install -g @scopedb/scopeview`) or invoke via `npx @scopedb/scopeview`:

1. Inspect the versioned schema contract: `scopeview schema --json`
2. Inspect built-in canonical documents: `scopeview example trace --json` (also `line`, `profile`, `scalar`, `bar`, `area`, `scatter`, `donut`, `top-list`, `treemap`)
3. Validate generated JSON before rendering: `scopeview validate --input report.json --json`
4. Render a standalone zero-dependency HTML report: `scopeview render --input report.json --output report.html --json`

## Data & Precision Invariants

- All document inputs follow the `version: 1` envelope (`id`, `kind`, optional `title`/`description`, and typed payload).
- Numeric values and timestamps can be encoded as strings so `int64`, `uint64`, high-precision decimals, and nanosecond epochs (`> 2^53 - 1`) survive JSON parsing without IEEE-754 rounding.
- Metric series preserve explicit `null` slots as data gaps instead of coercing missing samples to `0`.
- Trace spans preserve `startTimeNs` and `endTimeNs` exact nanosecond strings (including `1 ns` and `0 ns` spans), and CPU profiles preserve `BigInt` frame weights (`selfWeight`) alongside `file:line` metadata.
